title: Prepared-solve first-convergence versus fixed-response continuation diagnosis
question: Does the 7.235179122488944e-11 m G21A prepared-solve path effect persist when the exact same outer-2 affine response is supplied for additional MODFLOW solve calls after the first convergence report, or is it primarily a first-convergence-report/tolerance effect inside the continuous prepared solve?
experiment_contract: Build two independent live MODFLOW6 models from the identical accepted groundwater origin and identical timestep.
FRESH arm: open one prepared solve and apply only the frozen outer-2 response for exactly 12 successive solve calls, recording head and MODFLOW convergence flag after every call.

HISTORY arm: open one prepared solve; replay the frozen outer-1 lambda sequence, settling each lambda only to its first MODFLOW convergence report; then apply the exact same frozen outer-2 response for exactly 12 successive solve calls, recording head and convergence after every call.
Do not mutate X or XOLD directly, do not reopen or reconstruct either prepared solve, and keep the published outer-2 HCOF/RHS bitwise constant within each 12-call tail.
Require accepted XOLD bitwise fixed after every solve call.

Record the first convergence call in each outer-2 tail but deliberately continue the same response after that report for diagnostic purposes; F-GC39 already permits further external solve calls when coupled convergence is not yet satisfied.
At the end of the fixed 12-call tail, finalize_solve exactly once and do not finalize_time_step.
No SWAP trial, E3, P4 merit decision or coupling acceptance decision is performed in G21B; the experiment isolates the groundwater prepared-solve path.
quantitative_gates: The HISTORY outer-1 replay reproduces all three G20 settled lambda heads within 1e-12 m.
The FRESH outer-2 first convergence occurs by call 12 and its first-converged head is within 1e-12 m of the frozen fresh reference.
The HISTORY outer-2 first convergence occurs by call 12 and reproduces the G21A first continuous convergence head within 1e-12 m.
Both arms keep XOLD bitwise fixed and use one prepare_time_step plus one prepare_solve only.
The outer-2 response HCOF/RHS is unchanged for all 12 tail calls in both arms.
Report head error to the frozen fresh reference after every tail call, including calls after the first convergence report.
Report whether additional same-response solve calls reduce the HISTORY path effect below 1e-12 m by call 12.
Report final HISTORY-minus-FRESH head difference after 12 outer-2 calls.
Exactly one finalize_solve and zero finalize_time_step calls per arm.
No production runtime or adapter source is changed.

interpretation_rules.first_convergence_tolerance_dominated: HISTORY first-convergence error exceeds 1e-12 m but additional identical-response solve calls reduce |HISTORY-fresh_reference| to <=1e-12 m by call 12 and final HISTORY-minus-FRESH is <=1e-12 m.
interpretation_rules.persistent_prepared_path: HISTORY remains more than 1e-12 m from the fresh reference after 12 identical-response calls and final HISTORY-minus-FRESH remains more than 1e-12 m.
interpretation_rules.mixed_or_other: The two arms or convergence sequence do not support either bounded classification; preserve measured trace without policy inference.

pass_interpretation: PASS is diagnostic only: it classifies whether the G21 path effect is removed by continued identical-response solve calls or persists across the fixed tail. It does not alter the admitted meaning of MODFLOW convergence, and it does not create a new coupling convergence rule.
fail_interpretation: Preserve failure. Do not change the 12-call tail, response parameters, solver tolerances, G21/G21A evidence or F-GC38/F-GC39 semantics after seeing results.
